entries.name: NIDAP — National Integrated Digital Agriculture Platform
entries.lead: FMAFS — Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, with FAO technical support
entries.scale: Design/inception stage — inception workshop held Lagos, 7–9 May 2025; validation workshops through 2025; platform not yet deployed
entries.results: None — pre-implementation; FAO/FMAFS communications describe steps 'toward the establishment' of NIDAP
entries.verification_note: Status DOWNGRADED from starter's 'Adopted': all 2025 sources (FAO, Daily Trust 22 May 2025, Independent Jul 2025) describe establishment as prospective; no adopted programme document or deployment evidence found. fao.org maps to T1 in the starter domain lookup, but a country-office news item is treated as T4 grey communication here — admissible for existence.

entries.name: National Digital Agriculture Strategy 2020–2030 (NDAS)
entries.lead: NITDA — National Information Technology Development Agency, with FMARD (predecessor ministry); informed by the FAO–ITU e-agriculture framework
entries.scale: Policy blueprint — 47-page draft issued by NITDA in 2020; never formally adopted or gazetted; an NDAS review workshop was reported in Nov 2025 alongside the FAO-supported NIDAP work
entries.src: Degila et al. (2023), 'Digital Agriculture Policies and Strategies for Innovations in the Agri-Food Systems', Sustainability 15(12):9192 — reviews the strategy's status and attributes the 2020 draft to NITDA (accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: Lead CORRECTED from starter's 'FMAFS with FAO and ITU support': bibliographic records consistently cite 'Nigeria Digital Agriculture Strategy (2020–2030); NITDA: Abuja, 2020; 47p', and a 2025 journal cites it as a draft hosted on nitda.gov.ng. Adoption status could not be checked on government domains (fmard.gov.ng unreachable — HTTP 525 — on 2026-08-22).

entries.name: Growth Enhancement Support / e-Wallet (GES)
entries.lead: FMARD (Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, predecessor ministry) + Cellulant
entries.scale: 4.5M+ farmers received subsidized inputs via e-wallet vouchers, 2012–2017 (program-reported; totals vary across programme and literature sources and were never independently audited)
entries.results: Independent studies document input-access, yield/output and rural-enterprise gains; network failures, elite capture and exclusion of the poorest are also documented. Succeeded as the input e-voucher vehicle by NAGS-AP (2023– )
entries.src: Uduji & Okolo-Obasi (2019), EJISDC 85:e12066 (Wiley); corroborated by Alabi et al. (2020), AERC Research Paper 390 (accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: Two independent T2 confirmations of results direction (second: https://aercafrica.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Research-Paper-390.pdf). The 4.5M scale figure is programme-reported and carried with that flag; some sources claim up to 10.5M registrations — not verified, not used.

entries.name: Anchor Borrowers' Programme (ABP)
entries.scale: CBN-reported: ₦1.12tn disbursed to ~4.67M farmers via 563+ anchor firms, 2015–2023; new disbursements halted from late 2022 and CBN exited direct development-finance interventions in 2023
entries.results: Auditor-General audit of CBN's 2022 accounts found ₦629.04bn outstanding/unrecovered at end-2022 and weak internal controls; House of Representatives probe of alleged diversion of the ₦1.12tn ongoing (launched Nov 2025, continuing 2026). CBN's rice-output claims remain unverified by independent sources
entries.src: CBN ABP programme page (existence); Auditor-General findings as reported by Premium Times, 30 Nov 2025 (accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: Existence link: https://www.cbn.gov.ng/DFD/agriculture/ABP.html. Results tier T3 rests on the Auditor-General report (official) — the resolvable deep link is press coverage of it (T5 carrier); archived copy pending. Beneficiary counts vary by source (4.67M per probe records; 'at least 4.8M' per audit coverage) — all CBN-reported.

entries.name: NIRSAL — Nigeria Incentive-Based Risk Sharing System for Agricultural Lending
entries.lead: Central Bank of Nigeria (owner); NIRSAL Plc
entries.scale: ₦136.65bn cumulative bank financing facilitated for agriculture, principally via Credit Risk Guarantees (institution-reported, mid-2026); ₦100bn+ in guarantees approved in 2025 alone (institution-reported)
entries.results: No independent effectiveness evaluation located; facilitation figures are self-reported activity metrics, not impact evidence. CBN dissolved NIRSAL's previous MD/board in Aug 2024; operations continue under new management
entries.src: NIRSAL Plc mid-year performance statement, Aug 2026 (corporate site — existence and self-reported scale only; accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: Scale CORRECTED DOWN from starter's '₦200bn+': NIRSAL's own Aug 2026 statement puts cumulative facilitated financing at ₦136.65bn; older larger claims mixed instruments. 2024 proposals to merge NIRSAL MFB with the Bank of Agriculture (National Council on Privatisation, Apr 2024) not consummated as of Aug 2026 — treated as unverified. NIRSAL is within scope of the House ₦1.12tn probe (NIRSAL MFB reportedly disbursed ₦215bn).

entries.name: FADAMA III (Third National Fadama Development Project)
entries.lead: World Bank / FMARD, implemented in all 36 states + FCT
entries.scale: US$250M IDA credit (US$235M disbursed); 39,715 Fadama User Groups with ₦11.5bn in acquired assets at core-project completion (Dec 2013); closed 31 Dec 2019 after two additional financings
entries.funding: World Bank IDA credit + federal/state/local counterpart
entries.results: ICR (Nov 2016): beneficiaries' average real income +20% at closure (nominal +62%; target 40% real); average yield gains of 29.7% across nine crops; 87.9% beneficiary satisfaction; outcome rated Moderately Satisfactory
entries.src: World Bank, Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003895, 2 Nov 2016 (accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: Starter's '60k+ user groups' NOT supported by the ICR — corrected to 39,715 FUGs (ICR data sheet, verified against the PDF). ICR is a Bank self-evaluation; protocol treats donor completion reports as T2 where independently validated (IEG reviews ICRs) — flagged for §13.6 judgement.

entries.name: SAPZ — Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones
entries.lead: AfDB (African Development Bank) + federal and state governments; co-financiers include IFAD and IsDB
entries.scale: Phase 1 in implementation across 7 states + FCT (Cross River, Imo, Kaduna, Kano, Kwara, Ogun, Oyo per AfDB documents); Phase II first tranche (US$200M, approved 1 Dec 2025) covers 10 further states within a plan to reach the remaining 27 states — programme-reported
entries.funding: AfDB-led co-financing (Phase II via Multi-Tranche Financing Facility)
entries.results: Infrastructure build-out stage; no outcome evidence yet — AfDB job figures (1.1M jobs across the 10 tranche-1 states) and the US$1.5bn private-investment figure are ex-ante projections, not results
entries.src: AfDB press release, 4 Dec 2025 (accessed 2026-08-22); official programme site sapz.gov.ng
entries.verification_note: Phase II approval verified against afdb.org (Board approval 1 Dec 2025). Programme document deep link: https://www.afdb.org/en/documents/nigeria-nigeria-special-agro-industrial-processing-zones-phase-ii-sapz-ii-p-ng-aag-011. Status raised to Operating on the strength of AfDB-documented construction underway; zone-level operational evidence still thin.

entries.name: NiMet climate advisories / DCAS (Digital Climate Advisory Services)
entries.scale: National Seasonal Climate Prediction institutionalized — 2026 SCP unveiled 10 Feb 2026 with downscaled agromet advisories; rural last-mile penetration still reported limited
entries.results: Annual SCP production and public dissemination verified through the 2026 cycle (stakeholder validation Dec 2025, national unveiling Feb 2026); independent evidence on farm-level use and impact not located
entries.src: NiMet, '2026 Seasonal Climate Prediction' unveiling, 10 Feb 2026 (accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: SCP document deep link: https://nimet.gov.ng/publication_detail?id=71. The 'last-mile reach is the gap' judgement is narrative (T4/T5 commentary), not a scored claim.

entries.name: NAGS-AP — National Agricultural Growth Scheme–Agro-Pocket
entries.lead: FMAFS — Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security; partners: AfDB, JICA, NIMC, NAERLS
entries.scale: GES-successor digital input-subsidy scheme (2023– ): NIN-validated farmer registration and mobile e-vouchers redeemable at certified agro-dealers. AfDB-reported ~650,000 smallholder farmers reached in Phase 1; FMAFS-reported 80,000 wheat farmers registered for 2025/26 across 16 states; 2026 enrolment ongoing — programme/government-reported
entries.funding: Federal budget + AfDB (Phase 1 under AfDB emergency food production support; Phase 2 US$200M AfDB loan reported approved Feb 2026 — single trade-press source)
entries.results: No independent evaluation located. Government claims 2,536,184 tonnes of output worth ₦2.31tn across four seasons (Minister of State, Feb 2026) — official claim, not admissible as outcome evidence under the protocol (T3 does not cover outcomes)
entries.src: FMAFS release, 19 Nov 2025 (wheat flag-off, NAGS-AP registration figures); official portal nags-agropocket.ng (accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: NEW ENTRY (was missing from starter). Existence triple-confirmed: official portal (https://nags-agropocket.ng/about-us/), FMAFS releases, AfDB Phase-2 reporting. Government output claim deep link: https://ndfrplatform.ng/2026/02/10/nags-ap-delivered-2-5m-tonnes-of-agricultural-produce-worth-n2-31trn-in-four-years-hms/. AfDB Phase-2 US$200M: https://agrifocusafrica.com/2026/02/17/african-development-bank-group-approves-200m-for-nigerias-agricultural-expansion/ (T5, single source — AfDB's own release not located; archive pending).

entries.name: NDFR — National Digital Farmers Registry
entries.lead: FMAFS with NIMC (NIN anchor); IFAD and Heifer International supporting under the FG–IFAD Digital Innovation Action Plan
entries.scale: Registry under construction — NIN-anchored unique farmer identification; policy dialogue launched May 2025; multi-stakeholder learning/knowledge platform launched Nov 2025; no published farmer count yet

entries.src: The Guardian (Nigeria), 22 Nov 2025, coverage of the FMAFS/IFAD/Heifer NDFR capacity-building workshop (existence only; accessed 2026-08-22)
entries.verification_note: NEW ENTRY. What launched in Nov 2025 is a knowledge-exchange/learning platform to support building the registry, not a populated registry — hence Adopted, not Operating. Platform site: https://ndfrplatform.ng. Data-protection/ONSA involvement stated by the Minister. Archive of T5 link pending.

entries.name: Tingo Mobile / NWASSA
entries.scale: Claimed 9M+ farmer-subscribers at peak — vendor-reported figures the US SEC alleges were fabricated (reported US$461.7M Nigerian cash balances against an actual combined balance under US$50; 'fabricated the customer relationships that formed the basis of their purported businesses')
entries.results: US SEC fraud charges and emergency asset freeze against founder Dozy Mmobuosi and three Tingo entities (complaint filed 18 Dec 2023); parallel DOJ (SDNY) criminal charges Jan 2024. Included as documented evidence that headline Nigerian agritech farmer counts can be wholly unreliable
entries.verification_note: NEW ENTRY, cautionary. SEC page verified live 2026-08-22. SEC/DOJ artefacts are regulator documents (T3). Allegations remain allegations; what is established is that the vendor-reported farmer base cannot be treated as evidence — directly relevant to how this register weighs private-platform counts.

overlap_finding: Farmer registration remains the register's structural overlap, and it has deepened since the starter pass. Closed programs enrolled millions in silos — GES 4.5M+ (program-reported), ABP ~4.67M (CBN-reported) — and the pattern is repeating: NAGS-AP has been re-registering farmers since 2023 (NIN-validated, ~650k reached per AfDB in Phase 1; 80k wheat farmers for 2025/26 alone), while private platforms claim millions more (ThriveAgric 1.2M+, Crop2Cash 500k+ — vendor-reported, and the Tingo fraud case shows such counts can be fabricated outright). Yet the national registry (indicator 3.3) records only a fraction of farming households. The government now concedes the fragmentation explicitly: the National Digital Farmers Registry (NDFR, Nov 2025) was launched precisely because — in the Minister's framing — duplicated, inconsistent databases have caused resource leakage. NDFR is the announced fix (NIN-anchored, NIMC-backed), but as of Aug 2026 it is a design-stage commitment with no published farmer count; NAGS-AP's NIN-validated rolls are the closest thing to a functioning registry and are program-owned, not national. Enrollment keeps happening; a registry still has not.
